put.description:
Turn pairing on or off (owner's request, 2026-09-09: loginless by
default, with a way back for a more cautious operator).

``ControlDep`` gives this the asymmetry the setting needs without any
extra check: with auth already off, ``ControlDep`` is a no-op, so any LAN
caller can turn pairing *on* — harmless, it only adds protection. With
auth on, ``ControlDep`` demands a real control session, so nobody can turn
it *off* without already being paired.

Turning it **on** mints a fresh session for *this* caller and sets its
cookie before the new requirement takes effect on the very same response,
so the browser making the change is not locked out of it — every other,
not-yet-paired device is the one that now has to pair. Turning it off, or
leaving it unchanged, touches no session: existing sessions are left
exactly as they were in both directions, because neither transition makes
a session that was legitimately issued any less so.

same 409-if-unset guard the rest of this module uses rather than a
silent fallback to the geocentre.

get.description:

post.description:
When in the year is this target actually worth imaging — one summary
sample per night over ``body.nights`` consecutive nights starting at
``body.start_time`` (DESIGN.md 4.4): the target's peak apparent altitude
during astronomical darkness, when that peak occurred, and how many hours
it spent above ``body.min_altitude_deg`` while it was dark. This is the
yearly counterpart to ``/night``'s per-night altitude curve — a POST, like
``/night`` and unlike ``/moon-altitude``, because the body carries a
target's RA/Dec rather than just a time window.

A night with no astronomical darkness at all (high latitude, midsummer)
or where the target never clears the limit is reported honestly rather
than as a guessed zero — see ``ssc.astro.events.AnnualAltitudeNight``.

"Best targets tonight" (DESIGN.md 3.5): the top ``body.top_n`` bundled
catalogue targets for the night in ``[body.start_time, body.end_time]``,
ranked by how good *this* night actually is for each of them — Moon
altitude, illumination and separation weighed against whether the
target's light is the narrow emission lines the Seestar's own
dual/multi-narrowband filter passes, not Moon phase alone. See
``ssc.astro.best_targets`` for the full scoring model and the reasoning
behind it; every result carries the component values that produced its
score, never a bare number.

AbsoluteTimeSpec.title: AbsoluteTimeSpec
AbsoluteTimeSpec.description:
A wall-clock time authored by the user, e.g. ``2026-08-28T23:15`` local.

``local_datetime`` is naive on purpose: the zone is a property of
*Settings*, not of the plan, so the same plan compiles correctly at a
different site. ``fold`` picks which of the two instants an ambiguous
autumn reading (01:30 occurring twice) means — ``0`` for the first
(pre-transition) occurrence, ``1`` for the second — and is meaningless,
but harmless, on a unique or nonexistent reading.

AlpacaDeviceItem.description:
One device ``ssc-alpaca`` currently serves, for the connections footer.

``connected`` is genuinely tri-state (CLAUDE.md invariant 7): ``True`` or
``False`` is what the device's own ``Connected`` member answered:
``None`` means SSC could not ask it at all — a bounded read timed out, or
the request failed in transport — never a guess standing in for either
real answer.

Measured live, 2026-09-10: ``Connected`` is **not a health signal** on
this device. While the mount was wedged, ``telescope/0/connected`` read
``true`` while every other member on it refused with ``NOT_CONNECTED``;
later it read ``false`` while those same members worked. So this field
means exactly "the device reports ``Connected``", nothing stronger — it
must never be read as "this device is working".
AlpacaDeviceItem.title: AlpacaDeviceItem

AlpacaDevicesState.description:
Every device ``ssc-alpaca`` serves, polled on the same tick as mount
telemetry (``ssc.main.AlpacaDeviceGateway`` — not a second loop) so a
desktop and a phone never disagree about which devices are connected,
the same requirement DESIGN.md's state design exists to satisfy for the
mount itself.

``stale`` mirrors :attr:`MountState.stale` exactly, including why it is a
plain field rather than a ``@computed_field`` — see that docstring.
The gateway publishes expiry transitions even when a poll is blocked.
:func:`refresh_devices_staleness` also refreshes the flag for REST and
WebSocket snapshots, as for mount telemetry.
AlpacaDevicesState.title: AlpacaDevicesState

``suspended`` is the modelled intent of an explicit user disconnect: it is
never inferred from :class:`LinkState`, because a deliberate disconnect and
an unexpected drop must stay distinguishable — only the former means "stay
disconnected until asked otherwise".

does not imply an optically settled image.

BodiesResponse.description:
``GET /api/astro/bodies`` — the Sun, the Moon and seven planets at one

BodyId.title: BodyId
BodyId.description:
The closed set of solar-system bodies SSC reports. Earth is absent for
the obvious reason; Pluto is absent because it is 14th magnitude and the
sky map has nothing useful to say about it.

BodyKind.title: BodyKind
BodyKind.description: How a client should draw the thing: a disk to scale, or a marker.

BodyPositionModel.title: BodyPositionModel
BodyPositionModel.description:
One solar-system body at one instant, for the sky map's Sun/Moon/planets
layer (``ssc.astro.bodies``, which states every convention below).

**Topocentric**, computed from the active location — not geocentric. The
Moon's parallax reaches ~1 deg, twice its own diameter, so this is the
difference between drawing it in the right place and the wrong one.

**Apparent place referred to the J2000 (ICRF) frame**: light-time,
deflection and aberration applied, frame *not* precessed to the equinox
of date. That matches ``TargetResolutionResponse``, ``BrightStarModel``
and ``ConstellationBoundariesResponse``, so the sky map can draw all four
in one coordinate system.

BodyTargetSpec.title: BodyTargetSpec
BodyTargetSpec.description:
A solar-system body named, never located (DESIGN.md 3.6).

**The Sun is refused here, not merely absent.** A plan document is portable
JSON and therefore untrusted input: it can be hand-edited, imported, or
written by another tool. ``_refuse_the_sun`` runs
:class:`ssc.astro.targets.BodyTarget`'s own constructor so that this layer
can never drift from the resolver's rule, and re-raises as a ``ValueError``
so the refusal arrives as an ordinary validation error (a 422 at the API
boundary) carrying the full reason rather than as a 500.

There is deliberately **no tracking-rate field**. DESIGN.md 3.6: "A body
target and its tracking rate are one decision, not two" — the rate is a
function of the body (:func:`ssc.astro.targets.tracking_rate_for_body`), so
the document has no way to express a wrong one.

BrightStarModel.title: BrightStarModel
BrightStarModel.description:
One named bright star (``ssc.astro.stars``, offline, no network) —
a point, unlike ``FieldObjectModel``: no size, orientation or type, just
a name, position and magnitude.

BrightStarsResponse.title: BrightStarsResponse
BrightStarsResponse.description:
The bundled named bright stars within a cone, brightest first —
``GET /api/astro/stars``. Static data for the process lifetime, like
``ConstellationBoundariesResponse`` above; one credit line for the whole
table (CC BY 4.0, IAU Working Group on Star Names), never a literal
string in the UI.

BulkCutoutJobState.description:
One bulk target-field cutout prefetch, live or historical
(``ssc/skymap/bulk_prefetch.py``) — a queue of individual
:class:`CutoutState` jobs over a scoped catalogue subset. Per-pair status
is never kept here (it would be hundreds of rows for one job); only the
aggregate a progress bar needs. Why any one pair failed or was skipped is
in the server log, not the snapshot.
BulkCutoutJobState.title: BulkCutoutJobState

BulkCutoutJobStatus.description:
Mirrors :class:`PrefetchJobStatus` minus ``UNAVAILABLE`` — that is a
per-pair outcome here (folded into ``BulkCutoutJobState.failed``), not a
whole-job one.
BulkCutoutJobStatus.title: BulkCutoutJobStatus

BulkCutoutScope.description:
What a bulk cutout prefetch covers. Deliberately not "everything" —
the bundled catalogue is ~13,324 objects, far too many to fetch in bulk
even respecting the one-request-per-host etiquette, and SDSS/Legacy
Surveys have no documented bulk-use policy (THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md, "Endpoint
gate"). Scoped to the object sets a user would plausibly image.
BulkCutoutScope.title: BulkCutoutScope

count.title: Count
count.description: Frame count; UI quality defaults are 100 bias, 50 dark, 30 per flat filter.

CalibrationCaptureStartRequest.title: CalibrationCaptureStartRequest
CalibrationCaptureStartRequest.description: Start one server-owned dark/bias set or per-filter flat run.

CalibrationRunState.description: Server-owned progress for an automatic bias or per-filter flat set.
CalibrationRunState.title: CalibrationRunState

CalibrationSummary.title: CalibrationSummary
CalibrationSummary.description:
Mirrors ``[calibration]`` in the profile TOML (DESIGN.md 3.2, 7). ``measured
= false`` is the honest default until a plate solve writes real numbers.

CameraFieldOfView.description:
The active camera's real field of view on sky, in degrees — read once
per connection (``ssc.main.AlpacaDeviceGateway``), not on every poll
tick, mirroring :class:`MountCapabilities`: a sensor's size and pixel
pitch do not change while connected, so there is nothing to gain from
re-reading them every second.

Computed from ``Camera.CameraXSize``/``CameraYSize`` (pixels),
``Camera.PixelSizeX`` (microns) and ``Telescope.FocalLength`` (ASCOM:
metres) via the standard small-angle field formula. Published only when
*all four* inputs were actually read from the device — there is no
half-known field (CLAUDE.md invariant 7): either ``width_deg``/
``height_deg`` are both known, or this whole section stays ``None`` on
:class:`StateSnapshot` and the sky map keeps its honest marker rather
than drawing a guess.

The axes are authoritative: observed ``CameraXSize=2160`` and
``CameraYSize=3840`` match the Seestar app's own portrait FITS
(``NAXIS1=2160``, ``NAXIS2=3840``). ``ssc.main`` therefore maps X to
width and Y to height directly; sorting the dimensions would rotate the
field overlay by 90 degrees.

``rotation_deg`` is the field's position angle on sky and is
independently optional even when the size is known: it is a property of
where the mount is pointing (it varied 87-105 degrees across the sky in
one night's measurements), not of the camera, and only a *recent* plate
solve can source it. ``None`` here means "no trustworthy rotation right
now", never "zero" — a caller must not draw it as due-north.
CameraFieldOfView.title: CameraFieldOfView

CaptureCalibrationItem.title: CaptureCalibrationItem
CaptureCalibrationItem.description:
``ssc.capture_calibration`` — darks matched to the session just imaged.
Scheduled *after* the lights (DESIGN.md 4.3), typically at nautical dawn
with ``FilterWheel.Position = Dark``.

CaptureConditionsModel.title: CaptureConditionsModel
CaptureConditionsModel.description:
SSC's own synthesis of cloud, moon and dew-point margin for tonight —
a judgement call, not a measurement. Never confuse with
``ForecastPointModel.transparency``/``seeing_arcsec`` (always ``None`` —
no shipped provider supplies either; see ``ssc.api.conditions``).

CaptureExposureRequest.title: CaptureExposureRequest
CaptureExposureRequest.description:
``POST /api/capture/exposure``'s pinned body — see the dispatch
contract. ``duration_s`` is validated against the camera's own
``ExposureMin``/``ExposureMax`` at request time, not here (those bounds
are per-device, read live — CLAUDE.md invariant 11's sibling rule).

``frame_type`` replaces the old ``light: bool`` — a dark and a flat are
both ``light=false``, and the folder template needs to tell them apart
(CLAUDE.md's capture contract change, 2026-09-10). Today's capture UI
only offers ``light``/``dark``; ``flat``/``bias`` are accepted here too
because the type is a closed, already-settled set — see
``ssc.capture.frame.FrameType``'s own docstring for why.

CaptureFilenameTemplateRequest.title: CaptureFilenameTemplateRequest
CaptureFilenameTemplateRequest.description: Filename stem template. SSC appends ``.fits`` after rendering.

CaptureFolderRequest.title: CaptureFolderRequest
CaptureFolderRequest.description:
``None`` clears the configured folder back to unset — capture then
refuses (409) rather than picking somewhere on its own (CLAUDE.md
invariant 11's sibling rule for storage).

CaptureFolderTemplateRequest.title: CaptureFolderTemplateRequest
CaptureFolderTemplateRequest.description:
Refused (422) at set time if it uses an unknown ``%PLACEHOLDER%`` or
renders to an absolute path or one that escapes via ``..``
(``ssc.capture.pathtemplate.validate_capture_folder_template``).

CaptureFrameQualityModel.title: CaptureFrameQualityModel
CaptureFrameQualityModel.description:
A catalogued frame's numpy-only HFR/FWHM star metric
(``ssc.capture.quality.FrameQuality``, ``ssc-bkv.8``). ``star_count=0``
means every size field is ``None`` — an empty or starless frame, never a
fabricated size (CLAUDE.md invariant 7). ``*_arcsec`` fields are
``None`` whenever the frame's FITS header carries no usable pixel
scale, even when the ``*_px`` fields are known.

CapturePathTagModel.title: CapturePathTagModel
CapturePathTagModel.description:
One ``%PLACEHOLDER%`` the capture folder template may use
(``ssc.capture.pathtemplate.PathTag``), with an example rendering so the
Settings UI never hardcodes the vocabulary.

CaptureSessionModel.title: CaptureSessionModel
CaptureSessionModel.description:
One contiguous run of frames on a target
(``ssc.capture.catalogue.Session``, DESIGN.md §9.5.4).

auto_lp_filter_for_emission_targets.title: Auto Lp Filter For Emission Targets

CaptureSettings.title: CaptureSettings
CaptureSettings.description:
Where SSC writes captured FITS frames (DESIGN.md §9.5.2).

``None`` until the user chooses one — deliberately not derived from
``AppConfig.data_dir``. This is the one place SSC writes gigabytes a
night, so a user will want it on a specific external disk, and it must
never silently default to whatever partition holds the app's own
database (CLAUDE.md invariant 11's sibling rule for storage). Validated
on the way in by :func:`ssc.settings.capture_folder.validate_capture_folder`
— this model itself does no I/O.

CaptureStage.description:
Where the in-flight capture operation actually is, each value backed
by a real device action — never a step that isn't implemented yet
(CLAUDE.md invariant 7). ``dithering`` includes the post-command mount
settle gate; exposure does not start until that gate succeeds.
CaptureStage.title: CaptureStage

CaptureState.description:
Whether SSC is mid-capture operation right now, and what the catalogue last
held (``ssc/api/capture_service.py`` drives the exposure; this is what a
desktop and a phone render of it — module docstring's own requirement,
applied to a second live-mutating surface after ``run``).

Populated at startup (``ssc.main.build_services``) from the catalogue's
own last complete frame, so ``last_frame_id``/``last_captured_at`` survive
a restart even though ``in_progress``/``last_error`` do not — mirrors
``secrets``' own "populated by the time any client can reach it" rule on
:class:`StateSnapshot`, not ``run``'s "``None`` until something has
happened" one.

``stage`` describes the current capture operation, including a dither and
its settle gate before the shutter opens. ``duration_s``/``started_at``
remain ``None`` during that phase and become known only once the exposure
starts. All operation fields are cleared back to ``None`` when it ends,
successfully or not — a client must never read finished-operation values
as if they still described a live one.
CaptureState.title: CaptureState

CatalogTargetSpec.title: CatalogTargetSpec
CatalogTargetSpec.description:
Fixed J2000 coordinates, as the Planning tab hands them over (DESIGN.md
3.4 boundary: RA in hours, Dec in degrees). This is what every plan item
carried before schema_version 2, and what a v1 document migrates into.

ClientConfigurationSettings.title: ClientConfigurationSettings
ClientConfigurationSettings.description: Portable durable browser preferences; interaction-only state stays local.

CometSuggestionModel.title: CometSuggestionModel
CometSuggestionModel.description: One time-resolved result from the bundled JPL SBDB comet snapshot.

CometTargetSpec.title: CometTargetSpec
CometTargetSpec.description:
A comet stored by durable JPL identity and source provenance.

Preview coordinates are intentionally absent. At execution the current
bundled snapshot must contain the same ``spk_id`` + ``designation`` pair,
pass the conservative orbit-quality guards, and be propagated for the
actual slew instant. ``snapshot_fetched_at`` records what the user selected
without pinning execution to that possibly older set of elements.

CompiledItem.title: CompiledItem
CompiledItem.description:
One item, resolved. ``start_utc`` is ``None`` iff the item's start could
not be resolved (unschedulable — never a guessed time, CLAUDE.md
invariant 7). ``end_utc`` is ``None`` if either that is true, or the start
resolved fine but the item's own ``end`` could not (its event never
occurs, or it resolves at or before the start) — same rule, applied to
the end independently. ``resolution``/``end_resolution`` are the human
echoes DESIGN.md 4.1 requires ("Astronomical dusk +15 → 22:47" /
"Astronomical dawn -30 → 04:12"): local for display, ``start_utc``/
``end_utc`` remain the truth.

CompiledPanel.title: CompiledPanel
CompiledPanel.description:
One slice of an item's time with its own pointing.

Two things produce these, and they are told apart by whether the centre is
known at compile time:

* a **mosaic panel** — ``row``/``col`` are its grid position and
  ``ra_j2000_deg``/``dec_j2000_deg`` its fixed sky centre; and
* a **body item's re-centring segment** — ``row``/``col`` are both ``0``
  and the coordinates are ``None``, because a solar-system body's position
  is a fact about an instant and the executor resolves it at the top of the
  segment (DESIGN.md 3.6, and see :data:`MAX_BODY_DRIFT_FRACTION_OF_FRAME`).

``None`` here means "not knowable until this runs", never zero
(CLAUDE.md invariant 7); nothing may read these two fields without
branching on it.

CompiledSchedule.title: CompiledSchedule
CompiledSchedule.description: ``Plan`` → this. Absolute UTC times, mosaics expanded, validated.

CompiledTarget.title: CompiledTarget
CompiledTarget.description:
The item's target, echoed for display (DESIGN.md 4.1: "the abstraction
must never hide what will actually happen").

For a catalogue target this is just the item's own fixed coordinates. For a
body it is **where the body will be at** ``resolved_at_utc`` — an estimate
for the UI and the Gantt, never what the executor points at: the executor
resolves the reference again at the moment each segment starts, which is the
entire reason the plan document stores a name rather than a position.

ConfigurationSettings.title: ConfigurationSettings
ConfigurationSettings.description:
Every portable non-secret settings section in one validated model.

Security and the secret-name registry are deliberately absent: importing
a backup must neither copy credentials nor unexpectedly lock out clients.

ConnectRequest.title: ConnectRequest
ConnectRequest.description: Omit both fields to connect to the remembered address.

ConstellationBoundariesResponse.title: ConstellationBoundariesResponse
ConstellationBoundariesResponse.description:
Every one of the 88 IAU regions' vertex rings, J2000, for drawing —
static data, safe for a long client-side ``staleTime``
(``ssc.astro.constellations`` module docstring: 1562 vertices, one file
read and precessed once per process).

ConstellationBoundaryRegionModel.title: ConstellationBoundaryRegionModel
ConstellationBoundaryRegionModel.description:
One IAU region's rings, already precessed to J2000 — see
:func:`ssc.astro.constellations.boundaries_j2000` for why this is a
fixed transform (no ``epoch``/``now``) and why the frontend must never
precess these itself.

ConstellationResponse.title: ConstellationResponse
ConstellationResponse.description:
Which of the 88 IAU regions a J2000 point falls in
(``ssc.astro.constellations``, offline, Delporte 1930 boundaries).

ConstraintsSpec.title: ConstraintsSpec
ConstraintsSpec.description:
DESIGN.md 3.4 ``constraints``. ``None`` means "no limit requested",
never zero.

ControlPinRequest.title: ControlPinRequest
ControlPinRequest.description: ``pin: null`` removes the PIN and returns every session to control.

CutoutDeleteAllResponse.title: CutoutDeleteAllResponse
CutoutDeleteAllResponse.description:
A local response model, not in ``ssc/api/schemas.py`` — that file was
mid-edit by a concurrent agent when this route was added; nothing here
is reused elsewhere, so a shared model would only be more to keep in
sync for no benefit.

CutoutJobStatus.description:
Mirrors :class:`PrefetchJobStatus`, plus ``UNAVAILABLE`` — the archive
itself answered and confirmed there is nothing here (off-footprint, or a
lookup step unreachable with no fallback route), which is not the same
as ``FAILED`` (an unexpected error worth a retry).
CutoutJobStatus.title: CutoutJobStatus

CutoutRequest.title: CutoutRequest
CutoutRequest.description:
Fetch a target-field cutout from one archive. ``size_deg`` is capped
at 6 — a field, not a survey (M11 spec). Every source but unWISE still
self-limits to 3 via its own request logic (``web/src/skymap/SkyMap
.tsx``'s ``MAX_CUTOUT_SIZE_DEG``); unWISE alone always requests exactly
this ceiling, deliberately more than the lens-fitted frame, so the map
can show framing context beyond the exact frame (``UNWISE_MAX_CUTOUT_SIZE
_DEG``, reported live 2026-09-07). Server-side, ``_fetch_unwise`` tiles
that one 6 deg request into a 2x2 grid of 3 deg sub-requests for sharper
imagery (reported live 2026-09-08) — an internal implementation detail,
still one job/one response from this endpoint's point of view. This
field is a shared upper bound, not a per-source guarantee — nothing here
enforces which source may ask for how much of it.

CutoutSourceModel.title: CutoutSourceModel
CutoutSourceModel.description:
One archive `POST /api/skymap/cutouts` may fetch a field from — listed
up front, credit included, so the panel can offer a "Fetch for this
field" row before any job exists (never a hardcoded label or credit
line in the frontend: ``THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`` requirement 4).

CutoutState.description:
One target-field cutout job, live or historical — the snapshot's
summary; the manifest (pieces, WCS) is fetched from ``GET
/api/skymap/cutouts/{id}`` when actually drawn.
CutoutState.title: CutoutState

CutoutWcsModel.title: CutoutWcsModel
CutoutWcsModel.description:
A linear (TAN/SIN-tangent-plane) WCS as the plain numbers the client
draws with — never an opaque object.

DeviceDescriptor.description: What SSC knows about one device. Carries no credential material.
DeviceDescriptor.title: DeviceDescriptor

DeviceEventRecord.description: One event pushed by the device, already redacted.
DeviceEventRecord.title: DeviceEventRecord

DeviceMountModeCheck.title: DeviceMountModeCheck
DeviceMountModeCheck.description:
Whether a *connected* device's live ``mount.equ_mode`` agrees with the
requested planning mode. Never used to decide ``mount`` — only to warn.

``checked`` is ``False`` whenever no live reading was available (nothing
connected, or the read failed): ``device_equ_mode`` and ``conflict`` are
then meaningless and must not be read as "no conflict" (CLAUDE.md
invariant 7 — unknown is not zero).

DeviceSettings.title: DeviceSettings
DeviceSettings.description:
The remembered scope addresses. Empty until discovery or manual entry.

``host`` remains the ordinary/Wi-Fi address for backward compatibility.
The persisted last healthy configured route is preferred, followed by
Ethernet and ``host`` as the automatic Wi-Fi fallback.

Diagnostic.title: Diagnostic
Diagnostic.description:
One finding against a plan or a compiled item — always with a reason
(CLAUDE.md: "every decision is logged with its reason"). ``item_id`` is
``None`` for a plan-level diagnostic that names no single item.

DiscoveryState.description: A LAN scan, in progress or finished. Bounded and cancellable.
DiscoveryState.title: DiscoveryState

DistortionModel.title: DistortionModel
DistortionModel.description: How faithful the rectilinear overlay is for this optic.

DitherSpec.title: DitherSpec
DitherSpec.description: Absolute, bounded dither range and frame cadence for an imaging item.

DurationEndSpec.title: DurationEndSpec
DurationEndSpec.description:
End ``minutes`` after the item's resolved start — the historical
``duration_min`` behaviour, now spelled as one kind of :data:`EndSpec`.

EthernetAddressRequest.title: EthernetAddressRequest
EthernetAddressRequest.description: Preferred wired endpoint; null host clears it and preserves Wi-Fi.

EventEndSpec.title: EventEndSpec
EventEndSpec.description:
End at a solar or lunar event plus an offset — e.g. astronomical dawn
minus 30 minutes. Same event vocabulary as :class:`EventTimeSpec`.

EventTimeSpec.title: EventTimeSpec
EventTimeSpec.description: A solar or lunar event plus an offset, e.g. astronomical dusk + 15 min.

ExternalToolModel.title: ExternalToolModel
ExternalToolModel.description: One optional process SSC can use without absorbing its licence.

FieldObjectModel.title: FieldObjectModel
FieldObjectModel.description:
One catalogue object inside a sky-map field (``GET /api/astro/objects``):
what the map needs to draw its outline. Size and orientation stay ``None``
when the catalogue has none — the map draws a circle or nothing, never a
guessed ellipse.

FilterItem.title: FilterItem
FilterItem.description:
``FilterWheel.Position``. ``position`` matches the ASCOM index-or-name
the driver accepts (e.g. ``"Dark"`` for the calibration shutter position).

FilterWheelPositionRequest.title: FilterWheelPositionRequest
FilterWheelPositionRequest.description: A zero-based index into the device-reported ``FilterWheel.Names``.

FilterWheelStateResponse.title: FilterWheelStateResponse
FilterWheelStateResponse.description:
Live ASCOM filter-wheel slots and current position.

``position == -1`` means the wheel is moving. Nullable readings retain
their device-supplied reason instead of being replaced with a guessed
slot or an empty list.

FixedCountSpec.title: FixedCountSpec
FixedCountSpec.description: A known integration: exactly ``frames`` frames, however long that takes.

FocuserMoveRequest.title: FocuserMoveRequest
FocuserMoveRequest.description:
``Focuser.Move`` — an absolute step position. No upper bound is
enforced here: ``Focuser.MaxStep`` is device-reported, not a constant
this schema may hardcode (CLAUDE.md invariant 11's reasoning applied to
focuser travel, not just an address).

FocuserPositionResponse.title: FocuserPositionResponse
FocuserPositionResponse.description:
``None`` when not connected or the device did not answer — never
guessed (CLAUDE.md invariant 7). ``note`` carries why, mirroring
``AlpacaDeviceItem.note``: ``position is None`` alone conflates "not
connected", "NotImplemented" and "the device timed out" into one
unexplained gap.

``step_size``/``step_size_note`` are the same shape applied to
``Focuser.StepSize`` (bead ssc-bkv.10) — a second, independent read, so a
device that answers ``position`` but not ``stepsize`` (this one, per
``ssc/alpaca/devices/focuser.py``: it declares ``StepSize`` unimplemented
rather than report a guessed microns figure) still gets an honest
position without ``step_size`` dragging it down to ``None`` too.

ForecastPointModel.title: ForecastPointModel
ForecastPointModel.description:
One timestamp's forecast, from exactly one provider — the wire shape of
:class:`ssc.weather.base.ForecastPoint`, minus ``seeing_arcsec`` and
``transparency``: both are always ``None`` from every shipped provider
(`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`), so they are omitted here rather than shipped as a
field that never carries anything.

FramingSpec.title: FramingSpec
FramingSpec.description:
DESIGN.md 3.4 ``framing``. ``lens`` names a profile optic id (``"tele"``,
``"wide"``) — resolved against the active scope profile at compile time,
never validated against a catalogue here.

FramingVisibilityModel.title: FramingVisibilityModel
FramingVisibilityModel.description:
Whether the framed target is actually visible over the horizon
profile, not just above some flat minimum altitude (DESIGN.md 5). A target
behind a roof is not visible, and claiming otherwise is the silent-wrong-
answer failure DESIGN.md 5 calls the worst this app has.

FromIntentRequest.title: FromIntentRequest
FromIntentRequest.description:
DESIGN.md 3.4's "Send to Scheduling" handoff: append one item built
from a ``TargetIntent`` to a stored plan.

HealthResponse.title: HealthResponse
HealthResponse.description:
Liveness. Deliberately uninformative to a caller with no session.

An unpaired device on the same Wi-Fi can reach ``/api/health`` — that is
the point of a liveness check — but it gets nothing beyond "the process is
up". ``seq``, ``database`` and ``device_gateway`` are filled in only for a
caller already holding a session cookie (CLAUDE.md invariant 8's LAN-security
counterpart, DESIGN.md §9): a filesystem path naming the OS username and
home-directory layout has no business answering an anonymous ``curl``.

HeaterAutomationSettings.title: HeaterAutomationSettings
HeaterAutomationSettings.description: Opt-in weather-driven dew-heater policy with explicit hysteresis.

HeaterItem.title: HeaterItem
HeaterItem.description:
``ssc.set_heater``.

DESIGN.md 4.3: "schedule by dew-point margin, not by clock" — as with
autofocus, evaluating a live dew-point margin is an executor concern;
the compiler resolves only the clock-based fallback ``start``.

HeaterStateResponse.title: HeaterStateResponse
HeaterStateResponse.description: Live state of the dew heater exposed as Alpaca ``Switch/0``.

HistoricalFrameSummary.title: HistoricalFrameSummary
HistoricalFrameSummary.description: Totals over unique retained catalogue frames, never exposure intents.

HorizonIntervalModel.title: HorizonIntervalModel
HorizonIntervalModel.description:
One continuous stretch during which a target is clear of the horizon
mask (``ssc.astro.events.VisibilityInterval``) — a target can clear a
treeline, be blocked by a chimney and re-emerge, so this is always a list,
never flattened to a single rise/set pair (DESIGN.md 5).

HorizonPointFix.title: HorizonPointFix
HorizonPointFix.description:
One stored vertex of the site's skyline mask (DESIGN.md 5).

Ranges mirror :class:`ssc.astro.horizon.HorizonPoint` except altitude's
floor: ``-10`` rather than ``-90``, because a stored obstruction point
below roughly "the observer is in a pit" is certainly a typo, not a real
treeline, and the API should say so rather than accept it silently.

HorizonRequest.title: HorizonRequest
HorizonRequest.description:
At least two points, no duplicate azimuth — the same rules
:class:`ssc.astro.horizon.HorizonProfile` enforces, checked here too so the
rejection names the fix rather than surfacing as an opaque 422 from deep
inside the astro core.

HorizonSettings.title: HorizonSettings
HorizonSettings.description:
The site's per-azimuth altitude mask: trees, roofs, the neighbour's
floodlight (DESIGN.md 5).

``points`` is ``None`` when no profile has ever been recorded — *unknown*,
never an empty list silently standing in for "no obstructions anywhere"
(CLAUDE.md invariant 7). A recorded profile always has at least two points;
that is enforced at the API boundary (``ssc.api.schemas.HorizonRequest``),
not here, so a value already accepted and stored can still be read back
even if a future build tightens the rule.

LinkState.description: The state of the connection to the scope.
LinkState.title: LinkState

LinkStatus.description: The device connection, mirroring the session state machine.
LinkStatus.title: LinkStatus

LiveStackResetRequest.title: LiveStackResetRequest
LiveStackResetRequest.description: Calibration masters selected from the catalogue or uploaded store.

LocationFix.title: LocationFix
LocationFix.description: One source's answer to "where is the scope?".

LocationSettings.title: LocationSettings
LocationSettings.description: Every fix we hold, keyed by where it came from.

LocationSource.description: Where the active location came from — always shown (DESIGN.md §5).
LocationSource.title: LocationSource

LocationState.description: The active observing location, with its provenance attached.
LocationState.title: LocationState

MetNoContactRequest.title: MetNoContactRequest
MetNoContactRequest.description: ``None`` or blank clears the stored contact and disables Met.no.

MoonAltitudeSeriesResponse.title: MoonAltitudeSeriesResponse
MoonAltitudeSeriesResponse.description:
The Moon's own altitude, sampled uniformly across a window — the
Scheduling tab's grey moon curve (DESIGN.md 4.4). Distinct from
``NightResponse.altitude_curve``, which tracks a fixed-RA/Dec target,
not the Moon.

MoonImpact.title: MoonImpact
MoonImpact.description:
Why the Moon did or did not cost this target points tonight — the
single most useful "why" for a user weighing the ranking against their
own judgement.

MoonSensitivity.title: MoonSensitivity
MoonSensitivity.description:
How much a bright, high, nearby Moon costs a target of this type —
the classification :func:`moon_sensitivity_of` assigns every scoreable
:class:`~ssc.astro.catalog.ObjectType` to. See the module docstring for
the physical reasoning.

MosaicGridSpec.title: MosaicGridSpec
MosaicGridSpec.description:
DESIGN.md 3.3/3.4 ``mosaic``. Deliberately unconstrained here — the
``ra_num``/``dec_num`` >= 1 and ``overlap_pct`` in range checks live in
:func:`ssc.plan.validate.validate_plan` as diagnostics, not as a hard
parse failure, so a malformed grid can still be loaded, shown and fixed
in the UI rather than rejected outright.

MosaicItem.title: MosaicItem
MosaicItem.description:
``ssc.mosaic``. A ``"duration"``-kind ``end`` here is *per panel* — the
compiler lays panels out end to end, so the item's total span is
``panel_count * end.minutes``. An ``"event"``/``"target_event"`` ``end``
is not meaningful per-panel and is treated as no duration (0 min).

MountCapabilities.description:
What this mount will let a client ask of it — read once per connection
(``ssc.main.AlpacaDeviceGateway``), not on every poll tick, since these do
not change while connected. ``None`` throughout until the first successful
read; each field is independently ``None`` if its own member could not be
read, never a guessed or fabricated default (CLAUDE.md invariant 7).
MountCapabilities.title: MountCapabilities

MountCoordinatesRequest.title: MountCoordinatesRequest
MountCoordinatesRequest.description: Shared by ``/slew`` and ``/sync`` — both take exactly a target.

MountFrame.description:
The equatorial frame a driver declares through ASCOM ``EquatorialSystem``.

All five ``EquatorialCoordinateType`` values are members on purpose: an
unsupported frame must be *representable* so it can be refused with its own
name (:class:`UnsupportedMountFrameError`), not collapsed into "not J2000"
and then guessed at.
MountFrame.title: MountFrame

MountMoveAxisRequest.title: MountMoveAxisRequest
MountMoveAxisRequest.description:
``rate_deg_s: 0`` stops that one axis — the jog-button release, not a
separate verb. The bound here is the mount's own structural ceiling
(DESIGN.md §4.4b); the route also checks the live advertised cap, which
could in principle be lower.

MountState.description:
Where the mount is pointing, what it is doing, and what it can do.

Polled, never pushed (Alpaca has no event channel) — ``ssc.main``'s
``AlpacaDeviceGateway`` is the sole writer, publishing a fresh reading
every tick while connected. Every scalar is independently ``None`` when
its member could not be read on that tick; a failed read is never papered
over with the previous value (CLAUDE.md invariant 7).

``polled_at`` is the last tick that produced *this* reading — carried
through unmodified while the link is down, rather than reset, so the
fields keep their last known value and :attr:`stale` is what tells a
client to stop trusting them, rather than the snapshot silently going
blank.

``stale`` is a plain field, deliberately **not** a ``@computed_field``:
``MountState`` is event-sourced (carried by ``MountChanged`` and folded by
the pure reducer) and must stay exactly round-trippable — the reconnect
test in ``tests/api/test_ws_replay.py`` re-validates a replayed snapshot
with this same class, and ``extra="forbid"`` refuses a computed field as
input even though pydantic happily emits it as output. Whoever constructs
a fresh reading sets ``stale=False``. The gateway validates its acquisition
timestamp before publication and emits a stale transition when a retained
reading expires, independently of blocked or failed polls. Staleness is
also recomputed by :func:`refresh_mount_staleness` for ``GET /api/state``
and every WS ``snapshot`` frame. Clients render that server decision;
their display clocks cannot override it.

PolarAlignmentStartInfo.description:
Which start point this run used and the effective sweep geometry.

``step_deg`` and ``arc_span_deg`` apply to every mode. The remaining
planning fields are populated where SSC computed them (fully for
``BEST``, partly for ``SEESTAR``); ``None`` for ``CURRENT``/``EXPLICIT``
means that no visibility geometry was computed, not that it was lost.

PolarAlignmentStartMode.description:
Which of DESIGN.md §4.5's start points a run actually used —
``ssc.api.polar_alignment_service.PolarAlignmentService.start``'s
``start_point`` echoed back into the section so a client can show a
computed field was a compromise rather than let it pass silently
(CLAUDE.md invariant 7).
PolarAlignmentStartMode.title: PolarAlignmentStartMode

PolarAlignmentStartRequest.title: PolarAlignmentStartRequest
PolarAlignmentStartRequest.description:
``POST /api/mount/polar-alignment/start``'s body.

``point_count`` defaults to 3 over a 60-degree arc (30-degree steps) for a
fast initial measurement. Selecting five or more points adds residual
degrees of freedom for a stronger quality check.

``start_point`` is DESIGN.md §4.5's "Start point" setting: ``best`` (the
default, since 2026-09-11 — ``ssc.astro.polar.best_conditioned_field``),
``current`` (the mount's own current J2000 position — the old default,
and still the right answer for anyone whose sky is not clear),
``seestar`` (the official-app field: local hour angle +15 degrees and
apparent declination equal to site latitude), or
``explicit`` (``start_ra_hours``/``start_dec_deg``, both required
together). Declination is held fixed across every point either way
(``ssc.astro.polar``: rotate in RA only). Giving a coordinate while
``start_point`` is not ``explicit`` is refused rather than silently
picking one meaning (CLAUDE.md invariant 7) — likewise ``explicit``
with either coordinate missing. ``step_deg``'s **sign** is DESIGN.md
§4.5's "direction" setting (east/west) — there is no separate field for
it, since a negative step already rotates the other way
(``ssc.api.polar_alignment_service.PolarAlignmentService.start``'s own
docstring). ``gain`` is DESIGN.md §4.5's own setting too: applied once,
before the first exposure — unbounded here since the camera's own
``GainMin``/``GainMax`` are per-device and read live by the driver,
never guessed at in this schema (CLAUDE.md invariant 11's sibling rule).

PolarAlignmentState.description:
Where a polar-alignment measurement run is right now.

``status is None`` means no run has happened in the current observing night. Every
other field is whole-section replacement, mirroring ``CaptureState``
(that class's own docstring): a desktop and a phone must never disagree
about whether SSC is mid-run, which point it is on, or what the last
result was.
PolarAlignmentState.title: PolarAlignmentState

PolarAlignmentStatus.description:
Where a 3(+)-point polar-alignment measurement run is right now.

Published throughout the run, not only at the end (``ssc/api/polar_alignment_service.py``'s
own module docstring): a user standing at a tripod in the dark needs to
see it working.
PolarAlignmentStatus.title: PolarAlignmentStatus

PolarAlignmentVerdict.description: The next honest action after a completed full sweep.
PolarAlignmentVerdict.title: PolarAlignmentVerdict

PolarRefinementResult.description:
A JSON-safe projection of ``ssc.astro.polar.PolarRefinement``,
following ``PolarAlignmentResult``'s own precedent one level up: the
updated axis/error/correction figures from ``PolarRefinement.model``,
plus the refinement-specific figures alongside them so a client need not
reconstruct one from the other.

Unlike ``PolarAlignmentResult``, nothing here is ever ``None`` on success —
``ssc.astro.polar.PolarRefinement`` itself carries no optional field (it
has no three-point-style "nothing to measure" case), so there is no
residual-style gap to protect against a confident zero.
PolarRefinementResult.title: PolarRefinementResult

PolarRefinementStage.description: The observable camera/solver phase of a live PA refinement.
PolarRefinementStage.title: PolarRefinementStage

(``ssc.api.polar_alignment_service.PolarAlignmentService._sweep_model``)
and from a reference solve the loop takes for itself at the mount's
current, tracking-stopped pointing.

Where the live tripod-refinement loop (DESIGN.md M10) is right now.

Every refinement is differential from the *sweep* that started this loop
— never from a previous refinement (``ssc.astro.polar.PolarRefinement``'s
own comment on why chaining would compound the reference solve's own
noise). ``status is None`` means no refinement loop has run this
session. A fresh sweep (``PolarAlignmentService.start``) resets this
section: a new sweep invalidates whatever baseline the old refinement
measured against.
PolarRefinementState.title: PolarRefinementState

Where the live tripod-refinement loop is right now, mirroring

PolarRefinementStatus.title: PolarRefinementStatus

SessionEnvelopeModel.description:

them. Shapes 1-2 (the solid start rectangle and the ghost end rectangle) are

point, not just how many touch it) is not computed here: it needs a 2D
rasterisation ``ssc.astro`` does not provide (its radial arrays are a 1D
support function per angle, sufficient for the envelope/keep-region bound
but not for "how many frames overlap this pixel"). A client already
rasterising ``samples`` to draw the frame stack is the cheaper place to
accumulate that count than a second pass here — left to it rather than

SurveyModel.description: One registry entry plus its live availability and cache coverage.

SyncItem.description:
``Telescope.SyncToCoordinates``. Omit coordinates to sync to the last
plate solve instead of named target coordinates.

TakeExposuresItem.title: TakeExposuresItem
TakeExposuresItem.description:
**The exposure block** (DESIGN.md 4.3.0) — one item carrying every
parameter one imaging run needs.

> Owner, 2026-09-10: "i would like to have univerzal take exposures block
> within which we would configure how many or if until the end of block,
> what gain, what filter, which type, what exposure time, and dithering
> settings all withing the exposure block".

The block *sets* what it needs rather than inheriting it: the executor
issues this item's own filter, exposure and gain before its first frame,
every time. That is what makes a block reproducible in isolation, survive
reordering, and resume without archaeology — a few redundant property
writes per block cost nothing against a 30-second exposure, and the
alternative (``set_gain`` an hour ago, invisible here) is the state leak
that decomposition into verbs made inevitable.

``exposure_sec`` and ``gain`` are bounded by the *camera's own reported*
limits, never by a constant in this file: the check lives in
:func:`ssc.scheduler.compiler.compile_plan`, which takes them as
:class:`ssc.scheduler.exposure.CameraLimits` read from
``Camera.ExposureMin``/``ExposureMax``/``GainMin``/``GainMax``. Without
those limits the compiler says so as a diagnostic rather than assuming the
value is fine.

``filter_name`` is a ``FilterWheel`` position by name (``"Dark"``, ``"IR"``,
``"LP"`` on the S30 Pro). ``None`` means the block does not touch the
wheel — honest, but a state leak by definition, so
:func:`ssc.plan.validate.validate_plan` says so out loud.

TargetCenteringRequest.description: J2000 target plus bounded closed-loop pointing settings.

``rises_above`` / ``transits`` / ``sets_below`` for the item's own
target, as an end rather than a start. Same rule as

the compiler (and :func:`ssc.plan.validate.validate_plan`) reports a

TargetEventTimeSpec.description:

``mosaic``, ``slew``, or a ``sync`` with explicit coordinates) — the
compiler reports a diagnostic and marks the item unschedulable if not.
``alt_deg`` is required for ``rises_above``/``sets_below`` and must be
omitted (or ``None``) for ``transits``, which has no altitude of its own.

framing/mosaic/constraints the Planning tab worked out for it.

TargetIntentPanel.title: TargetIntentPanel
TargetIntentPanel.description: One zero-based panel centre calculated by the Planning backend.

TargetSuggestionsResponse.title: TargetSuggestionsResponse
TargetSuggestionsResponse.description: Ranked, de-duplicated matches from the bundled offline catalogue.

TonightWeatherRowModel.title: TonightWeatherRowModel
TonightWeatherRowModel.description: One evidence row behind ``conditions`` — never a substitute for it.

UntilBlockEndSpec.description:
Expose until the block's own window closes — "image this until it sets".

A block with this count **must** carry an ``end``: without one there is no

(CLAUDE.md invariant 7).

WeatherSettings.title: WeatherSettings
WeatherSettings.description:
Provider configuration the user can set from Settings.

Only Met.no's contact lives here. It is deliberately **not** a secret:
Met.no requires it to be sent in the ``User-Agent`` of every request, so
it is published by design and storing it in the keyring would imply a
confidentiality this value does not have. OpenWeatherMap's API key *is* a
secret and lives in the keyring under ``openweathermap_api_key``
(invariant 8) — this model never sees it.

``None`` means no contact has been set here; ``AppConfig.weather_contact``
(from ``SSC_WEATHER_CONTACT``) is then the fallback. A value stored here
wins, so that setting it in the UI visibly takes effect on a deployment
whose environment already carries one.

WeatherSettingsResponse.title: WeatherSettingsResponse
WeatherSettingsResponse.description: What is configured, never the OpenWeatherMap key itself.

WifiAddressRequest.title: WifiAddressRequest
WifiAddressRequest.description: Fallback wireless endpoint; null host clears it and preserves Ethernet.

ssc__capture__frame__FrameType.title: FrameType
ssc__capture__frame__FrameType.description:
What an exposure *is*, chosen by the user before capture — never
inferred from ``light``/``dark`` alone, because a dark and a flat are
both shutter-closed-or-not-relevant-to-ASCOM but land in different
folders and mean different things to a stacker.

All four are defined now, even though today's capture UI only offers
:attr:`LIGHT` and :attr:`DARK` (owner, 2026-09-10: "so far lights and
darks, in future flats via wizard and biases too"). Flats need a
procedure (panel or sky, per optic) and biases a zero-length exposure —
both are UI/workflow gaps, not gaps in what a frame's *type* can be, so
defining the closed set up front means the catalogue schema and the
folder layout never need a migration when flats/biases arrive.

ssc__plan__models__FrameType.title: FrameType
ssc__plan__models__FrameType.description:
What an exposure *is* — the same closed set, and the same wire strings,
as :class:`ssc.capture.frame.FrameType`.

Restated here rather than imported, for exactly the reason
:class:`ssc.store.capture.CaptureFrameRecord` restates it too: ``ssc.plan``
is pure (CLAUDE.md invariant 3), and ``ssc.capture``'s package ``__init__``
reaches ``ssc.store`` — importing it here would drag SQLite in behind the
plan document. The two enums are held to the same four values by
``tests/plan/test_models.py``, which may import both.

A dark is *not* a separate item kind: it is a ``take_exposures`` block with
``frame_type: dark`` through the ``Dark`` shutter position (DESIGN.md 4.3.0).

:class:`~ssc.state.models.CameraFieldOfView`). Unlike ``MountChanged``,
this is not re-sent on every tick: the geometry it carries is read once
per connection and does not change while connected.
CameraFovChanged.title: CameraFovChanged

FrameType.description:
What an exposure *is*, chosen by the user before capture — never
inferred from ``light``/``dark`` alone, because a dark and a flat are
